column1: # acmg_lof_overrides.tsv: the hand rows of the lof column of assets/acmg_sf.tsv, each with its reason.
# Hand-curated from ClinGen's gene curation list and the ACMG SF papers; reviewed like code.
# og dev build acmg-lof (scripts/ci/build-acmg-lof.sh) writes the lof cell of each ACMG gene: yes when
# ClinGen's haploinsufficiency score is 3 (sufficient evidence that losing one copy causes disease), no
# when it is 40 (dosage sensitivity unlikely), and the row below for every other gene. ClinGen's other
# scores (0, 1 and 2 for no, little or some evidence, 30 for a gene of a recessive disease, or no score
# when ClinGen has not curated the gene) do not say whether loss of function causes the disease ACMG lists,
# so such a gene needs a row here, and the build stops for a gene that has none. A row also overrides a
# score of 3 or 40 that belongs to another disease. Columns, tab separated:
#   gene    the HGNC symbol, as in acmg_sf.tsv
#   lof     yes: a predicted loss-of-function call (a VEP HIGH-impact record) counts; no: it does not,
#           and only a ClinVar P/LP variant counts; mark: it counts, with a note that loss of function is
#           a less certain cause of the disease
#   reason  why, in a few words
